thread.title: Apple Poaches Google's AI Chief

author: Daniel Liberto
title: Apple Poaches Google's AI Chief
text:
Apple Poaches Google's AI Chief Investopedia 3 hrs ago Daniel Liberto © John Smith Apple Poaches Google's AI Chief
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) just took a crucial step toward bolstering its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities, an increasingly popular technology that the company has previously been accused of underinvesting in.
The iPhone maker has hired Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) Google’s chief head of search and AI, John Giannandrea, to run its “machine learning and AI strategy.” Giannandrea, who was one of the main figures responsible for introducing AI to Google’s products, including its search engine, Gmail and digital assistant software, left his role at Google earlier in the week.
Apple confirmed the appointment of its first senior vice president of AI following an earlier report from The New York Times.
“Our technology must be infused with the values we all hold dear,” the company's CEO Tim Cook said Tuesday morning in an email to staff members obtained by The New York Times. “John shares our commitment to privacy and our thoughtful approach as we make computers even smarter and more personal.” (See also: Apple Slams Facebook on Privacy, Trustworthiness .)
Apple’s latest hire represents a huge coup for the Cupertino-California-based company. In previous years, the iPhone maker has been criticized for spending less than its peers on AI, a technology focused on creating software that enables computers to learn and improve functions on their own.
AI, which is critical in areas such as self-driving cars and voice assistants, is viewed as one of the most important technological breakthroughs in Silicon Valley. Critics point out that Apple has lagged behind competitors, adding that a lack of investment in AI is the reason why its digital assistant, Siri, is less powerful than rival products offered by Google and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN).
Giannandrea joined Google in 2010 after it bought out Metaweb, the startup where he worked as chief technology officer. After the takeover, Google began using Metaweb’s expertise to improve its search engine capabilities. In the years that followed, AI research became increasingly important for Google.
Programmer Jeff Dean, one of Google’s earliest employees, is set to replace the departing Giannandrea as the company’s AI chief. (See also: Apple Will Depend on Services for Revenue Growth: Morgan Stanley .)
